Both Mr. Barut and Ms. Tohumcu were appallingly terrible at detecting plagiarism. I’ve seen a lot of people doing their models by copying projects from Instagram and Pinterest and getting highly appreciated by instructors. 

It was crystal clear that Mr. Barut was not respecting the final jury by means of dress code. We were told that we were expected to present ourselves not only our models however, this was not something Mr. Barut applied to himself. He gave an impression to all of us that he was not respecting the university’s manners of the official assessment day.

His critics were inconsistent before and during the juries. A lot people were saying that their projects were approved before and got new kinds of criticism while the jury. It seems like his assessment qualities were inconsistent and constantly chanfing. It is impossible to comment about Ms. Tohumcu because all she did was staring at projects and walls during the jury.

It was quite shocking seeing Mr. Barut at the final jury when he started defending one of the student’s project. The owner of the project did not take the pain to explain herself, because instead Mr. Barut did an explanation for about 3-4 mins about aspects of the project which probably the owner had no idea about what he was talking about. This type of behavior is totally unacceptable and unfair because nearly all of us spent so much time on our rehearsal of our presentations but he did not contribute to any of us. I believe the responsibility of explaining one’s design should lie on student’s hands, not the instructors.

Ms. Tohumcu conveys content inaccuracies that contribute to making the content incomprehensible to the students.

P.S. They both have to learn the pronunciation of ‘variable’ and ‘pyramid’.
